record.summary: Senate initiative for a national AI law of public order and general observance covering public- and private-sector use of AI in Mexico. It would create a regulatory agency for the development, use and application of AI empowered to classify systems by risk level, issue technical guidelines and handle complaints; require providers to assess data-processing risks, manage personal data and keep information-security plans; prohibit deceptive data collection, profiling for political persecution and subliminal manipulation; address deepfakes and algorithmic discrimination; and provide for fines, suspension and market withdrawal.
record.notes: Presented in the Senate on 11 February 2026 by Sen. Karina Isabel Ruiz Ruiz (Morena) and referred to the joint committees on Legislative Studies and on the Analysis, Monitoring and Evaluation of AI in Mexico; the referral was published in the Gaceta del Senado of 11 February 2026 (LXVI Legislature, second year). The bill would also recognise neurorights, give users a right to object to automated processing that significantly affects their rights, and refer possible crimes to the Attorney General's Office (FGR). It is one of several dozen AI bills pending in the Mexican Congress; no general federal AI law had been adopted as of October 2026.

verification.note: The only stored source is a law-firm alert (Basham, Ringe y Correa, 26 Feb 2026); the date, sponsor, committee referral, status and the bill's content in the summary and notes rest on it, not on the Spanish text. The Senate gazette PDF of the initiative, linked from the alert, and the Secretaría de Gobernación's SIL tracking report are not stored: the SIL host fails TLS verification and robots.txt could not be checked, and senado.gob.mx returned HTTP 403 in earlier passes. An earlier pass read the SIL report live; it gave the title 'Que expide la Ley Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial', presentation on 11 Feb 2026 (LXVI Legislature, second year, second ordinary period), the referral published in the Senate Gazette of 11 Feb 2026 and the status 'pendiente en comisión(es) de origen', and says its contents lack official validity. The original_title is not in any stored file: the alert calls the bill the 'National Law to Regulate the Use of Artificial Intelligence', while the gazette file name reads 'Expide_Ley_Nacional_de_Inteligencia_Artificial'. The statement on other pending AI bills rests on earlier research and press reports, which also describe a separate draft 'Ley General para Regular y Fomentar la Inteligencia Artificial' by the Senate AI commission. No committee action on this initiative appears in the stored file.
